_comment: Which container a project's checks run in, per toolchain.
ONE copy, read by three callers that would otherwise each keep their own:
scripts/verify_stack_checks.py (which is where this list came from, and
which proves each image can actually run that stack's checks in CI),
services/commit-reviewer/sandbox.js (which runs them for real), and
agent/provisioning.py (which picks one when a project is onboarded).
A second inventory of the same thing is how the review dashboard ended up
labelling live models from a list deleted months earlier. Add a stack here
`default` is the agent's own sandbox image and stays the answer for a
project with no detected stack of its own -- Node and Python live in it,
which is what most projects here are. env is what that toolchain needs to
work with a read-only HOME and no network: a cache directory it can
Images are PULLED, not built, except rust: the official image ships
rustup's minimal profile with neither rustfmt nor clippy, so `cargo fmt`
fails asking for `rustup component add` instead of giving a verdict.

rust.build:
FROM rust:1
RUN rustup component add rustfmt clippy

elixir._env_comment: HOME inside the mounted workspace, not /tmp: Hex installs itself under HOME, and a per-check container would throw that away and ask to install it again on the next check.
